repo_notes.content: Audience and outcome: write a guided architecture handbook for contributors and coding agents. Help a reader understand the control plane, trace a task through the code, choose the right place to change behavior, and find the tests that protect it. Explain the problem and mental model before introducing symbols. Prefer a concrete example and a short causal explanation to exhaustive class, endpoint, package, or configuration inventories. Use plain language and define abbreviations on first use.

Evidence and document authority: use current implementation, schemas, configuration, public exports, and tests to establish what ships in the indexed revision. Read `doc/GOAL.md` and `doc/PRODUCT.md` for intent and `doc/SPEC-implementation.md` for the V1 policy contract; `doc/SPEC.md` provides longer-horizon context. Contributor instructions such as `AGENTS.md` are not implementation evidence. Explain material disagreements between code and policy instead of silently treating either as proof of the other. Plans, historical snapshots, proposed ADRs, prototypes, fixtures, and roadmap entries do not establish shipping behavior. Verify their claims against production wiring and distinguish implemented, gated/experimental, and proposed behavior.

Page contract: each subsystem page should explain the problem it solves, what it owns, its inputs and outputs, authoritative persisted state, and its boundaries with neighboring systems. Trace one representative flow through actual entry points. Include a compact 'Where to change it' map linking responsibilities to source, relevant regression tests with the behavior they protect, and practical investigation steps for characteristic failures. Cite the code that performs a decision or effect rather than an import list or unrelated file. A passing unit fixture does not establish live provider support. Parent pages should offer reading routes, boundary maps, or diagnostic routing instead of repeating all their children.

Navigation and scope: generate the 30 specified pages in their listed hierarchy. Use descriptive internal links to the owning page instead of duplicating detailed explanations across chapters. Link to `docs/docs.json` and the corresponding pages at https://docs.paperclip.ing for maintained user, command, and API reference; verify the route from the docs configuration rather than inventing URLs. Distinguish public product docs under `docs/`, engineering contracts under `doc/`, repository contributor skills under `.agents/skills/`, runtime coordination skills under `skills/`, and app-shipped skills and teams catalogs. Do not turn this handbook into a second exhaustive API manual.

Diagrams and worked examples: include an architecture diagram on Architecture and Repository Map, an end-to-end sequence on A Task from Request to Work Product, separate task and run state diagrams on Completion, Review, and Human Decisions and Run Agents respectively, and an authorization sequence on Connections, Credentials, and MCP. Label arrows with actions and identify process, persistence, and authority boundaries. Keep diagrams small enough to read, introduce them in prose, and cite their implementation sources. Explain conditions on transitions; do not infer transitions from an enum. Elsewhere add diagrams only when they clarify a relationship better than prose or a table.

Terminology and invariants: distinguish task (UI language) from issue (many APIs and tables), wake request from execution run, provider session from a run, business goals from session goals, project workspace from realized execution workspace, and parentage from a blocker or durable wait. Keep single-assignee ownership separate from active execution locks and review participants. Explain that successful execution does not by itself complete a task. Company isolation, checkout atomicity, governed approvals, budget enforcement, and mutation audit history belong to the control plane. Provider permission settings do not grant Paperclip authority, credentials, or cross-company access.

Freshness: resolve defaults, feature gates, supported providers, package exports, status values, and commands from the indexed code every time the wiki is generated. Source anchors below are starting points, not an exhaustive file allowlist; follow their production callers and adjacent tests. If an anchor moves, locate its replacement and cite that implementation, or explicitly identify removal. Do not invent a replacement symbol. Do not preserve hardcoded provider/version inventories or source line numbers from this configuration. Recheck direct-adapter versus experimental Paperclip Runner selection and persisted-run recovery behavior rather than assuming every agent uses Runner.

Diagnostic evidence and data destinations: clearly separate the local run log (`heartbeat_run_events`), operator-configured OpenTelemetry observability, and opt-out first-party telemetry. Explain where each is stored or sent, its enablement/default behavior, and which question it answers. Keep activity audit records and work-product artifacts distinct from those three paths as well. Use safe example identifiers, never actual credentials or private runtime data. For investigations, start with durable records and decision reasons; a comment, transcript claim, detached process, or local file alone is not proof of a healthy continuation, completed task, or delivered work product.
